subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human provenance contract and sensitive-target enforcement surface should OpenClaw support for exec, gateway mutations, and outbound messaging?
rationale: Source inspection shows the requested boundary is absent, but choosing the provenance semantics, config shape, plugin API exposure, and fallback behavior is a security/product decision rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Core gateway policy
options.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and denial or stricter approval fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

options.title: Plugin context first
options.body: First land hook context such as action classification and input provenance, then let a security plugin own the policy once the SDK contract is accepted.

options.title: Fold into taint design
options.body: Defer this request into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution guardrail design so maintainers choose one unified security model.

recommendation.title: Core gateway policy
recommendation.body: Add core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and denial or stricter approval fallback at the tool/gateway boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main routing signal for the plugin hook and policy contract surface points to vincentkoc.
